package.name: hugo-music
package.description: Frosted-glass UI kit with droplet motion for React Native and Expo — native and web

intro: Frosted-glass UI kit with droplet motion for React Native and Expo. One codebase for native apps and the web: translucent glass surfaces that blur what scrolls behind them, controls that squash and spring back like drops of water, and a calm layout system built on large titles, grouped lists and generous touch targets.

guide.title: Install
guide.body:
```
npx expo install hugo-music @expo/vector-icons expo-blur expo-glass-effect expo-linear-gradient react-native-safe-area-context
```

The peer packages provide icons, blur, the native glass material, gradients and safe-area insets. Nothing else is required; the kit has no other UI dependency. Import icons and gradients from the kit too (`Icon`, `Gradient`) so your app depends on a single UI package.

guide.title: Quick start
Frosted glass
guide.body:
`Glass` is the material under every floating control. It blurs and saturates what is behind it, adds a soft sheen on the upper half and a bright rim along the edge.

- **regular** — the default, for bars, toolbars and buttons.
- **clear** — thinner and more see-through, for controls floating over artwork or video.
- **tint** — colours the glass for prominent actions (a primary button, a selected state).
- **interactive** — the surface reacts to touch where the platform supports it.

Use glass for the layer that floats above content. Keep reading material — long text, lists, forms — on solid surfaces so it stays legible.

guide.title: Droplet motion
guide.body: Pressing a glass control squashes it (a little wider, a little shorter); releasing bounces it back on an under-damped spring, so it overshoots and wobbles before settling — like a drop landing on glass. Selection lenses in `SegmentedControl` and `GlassTabBar` slide on a spring and stretch while they move. `useDroplet()` exposes the same physics for your own components.

guide.title: Theming
guide.body:
- `useHugoTheme()` returns `{ isDark, colors }`: semantic colours (`background`, `surface`, `text`, `textSecondary`, `border`, `accent`…) plus the glass fills.
- `HugoProvider scheme="light" | "dark" | "system"` forces an appearance; `accent` overrides the brand colour per appearance.
- `renderArtwork` replaces how every cover is drawn — one place to route images through a CDN or a cache.

guide.title: Layout and spacing
guide.body: Tokens replace magic numbers: `space` (a 4-point grid), `radius`, `type` (Large Title 34 down to Caption 12), `TOUCH` (44-point minimum target) and `GUTTER` (content margin). `LargeTitle`, `Shelf`, `InsetGroup` and `ListRow` already apply them, so screens built from them line up without extra styling.

guide.title: Accessibility
guide.body:
- Icon-only controls take a required `label` that screen readers announce.
- Roles and states are set for you: tabs, selected items, adjustable date wheels, menus.
- Touch targets are at least 44 points.
- When the user asks for reduced transparency, glass becomes an opaque surface.

guide.title: Platform behaviour
guide.body:
| Where | Glass | Date picker | Context menu |
|---|---|---|---|
| Native, newest system glass | native glass material, interactive | wheels | glass menu |
| Native, other versions | system blur material | wheels | glass menu |
| Browsers | CSS backdrop blur with sheen and rim | browser date input | glass menu (long-press) |
| Native without blur | opaque fill | wheels | glass menu |

guide.title: Components
guide.body:
| Group | Components |
|---|---|
| Theme | `HugoProvider`, `useHugoTheme`, `useTone`, `space`, `radius`, `type`, `TOUCH`, `GUTTER`, `gradientFor`, `Icon`, `Gradient` |
| Glass | `Glass`, `GlassGroup`, `useDroplet` |
| Controls | `GlassButton`, `CapsuleButton`, `GlassCapsule`, `DropletPressable`, `ActionButton`, `SegmentedControl`, `Chips`, `Toggle`, `TextField`, `FormField`, `SearchField`, `DatePicker`, `ContextMenu`, `Spinner` |
| Navigation | `GlassTabBar`, `NavigationSidebar`, `BackButton`, `Sheet` |
| Layout | `LargeTitle`, `SectionHeader`, `Shelf`, `ListRow`, `InsetGroup`, `MediaTile`, `GradientTile`, `PinnedRow`, `GlassArt`, `Artwork` |
| Data display | `Card`, `StatCard`, `BarChart`, `Badge`, `EmptyState`, `Pager`, `ErrorText` |

Every component has its own page with props, usage notes, accessibility notes, examples and a live demo at `/developer/components` in the Hugo Music app.

components.name: HugoProvider
components.description: Optional root provider for the whole kit: picks the appearance, overrides the accent colour and plugs in your own artwork renderer. Every component works without it.

props.name: renderArtwork
props.description: Replaces the default artwork renderer (e.g. to route images through a CDN).

components.usage: Wrap the app once at the root when you need a light/dark switch of your own, a brand accent, or covers loaded through a CDN. Skip it to follow the device appearance with the default green accent.
components.remarks: Values travel through React context, so nested providers override outer ones — handy for previewing a section in the other appearance. `renderArtwork` replaces the image of every component that shows artwork (ListRow, MediaTile, Artwork).
components.a11y: The default palette keeps 4.5:1 contrast for text on backgrounds and for white text on the accent colour.

components.name: Glass
components.description: The frosted-glass material every control in the kit is built on: a translucent surface that blurs and saturates whatever scrolls behind it, with a sheen on the upper half and a bright rim along the edge.

props.name: radius
props.description: Corner radius; the default 999 makes a capsule.

props.name: variant
props.description: 'regular' for bars and controls, 'clear' (thinner) over rich media.

props.name: tint
props.description: Tints the glass (prominent buttons, selected states).

props.name: interactive
props.description: Reacts to touches (native interactive glass where available, press highlight elsewhere).

props.name: tone
props.description: Forces light or dark glass regardless of the app appearance (e.g. over dark artwork).

components.usage: Use glass for things that float above content — bars, toolbars, floating buttons, menus. Keep reading material (long text, lists, forms) on solid surfaces: glass over glass or text over busy glass loses legibility.
components.remarks: `variant="regular"` is the default material; `variant="clear"` is thinner for controls over rich media. `tint` colours the glass for prominent actions. On devices with a native glass material the kit uses it (interactive, reacting to touch); elsewhere it falls back to a system blur, CSS backdrop blur in browsers, or an opaque fill where no blur exists.
components.a11y: When the user asks for reduced transparency the glass becomes an opaque surface, so text on it stays readable.
examples:
<Glass variant="clear" tint="#0A84FF" radius={20} style={{ padding: 12 }}>
<Text style={{ color: '#fff' }}>Tinted, see-through</Text>
</Glass>

components.name: GlassGroup
components.description: Lays out several glass shapes together so that, where the platform supports it, neighbouring shapes melt into one another like drops of water joining.

props.name: spacing
props.description: Distance under which shapes merge (where supported) and the gap between children.

components.usage: Wrap a cluster of related floating controls — transport buttons, a toolbar — instead of placing separate glass buttons side by side.
components.remarks: `spacing` is both the gap between children and the distance under which shapes merge. Without native support it is a plain row (or column) with that gap, so layouts stay identical everywhere.
components.a11y: Grouping is visual only; every child keeps its own label and role.
examples:
<GlassGroup spacing={10}>
<GlassButton icon="play-skip-back" label="Previous" onPress={prev} />
<GlassButton icon="play" label="Play" tint={accent} onPress={play} />
<GlassButton icon="play-skip-forward" label="Next" onPress={next} />
</GlassGroup>

components.name: ActionButton
components.description: Capsule-shaped button in frosted glass with the droplet press effect.

props.name: title
props.description: Leave empty for an icon-only button (then pass accessibilityLabel).

props.name: variant
props.description: 'primary' tinted glass in the accent colour · 'glass' plain glass · 'danger' red text · 'plain' no background.

props.name: size
props.description: 'sm' 32 pt (toolbars, tables) · 'md' 44 pt · 'lg' 50 pt.

props.name: icon
props.description: An Ionicons glyph name, or any element (shown before the title).

props.name: loading
props.description: Shows a spinner instead of the icon and blocks presses.

props.name: tint
props.description: Overrides the accent tint of a primary button.

components.usage: The main action of a screen or sheet — Sign in, Continue, Save — with `variant="primary"` once per screen. Use `glass` for the secondary choice next to it (Cancel, Back), `danger` for destructive actions and `plain` for low-emphasis actions in toolbars and tables.
components.remarks: Primary buttons are glass tinted in the accent colour with white text. `size="sm"` (32 pt) suits dense tables, `md` is 44 pt and `lg` 50 pt. `icon` takes an icon name or any element; `loading` swaps it for a spinner and blocks presses. Without `title` it becomes an icon-only button.
components.a11y: The title is the accessible name; icon-only buttons need `accessibilityLabel`. Disabled and busy states are announced.
examples: <ActionButton variant="danger" size="sm" icon="trash-outline" title="Delete" loading={deleting} onPress={remove} />

components.name: CapsuleButton
components.description: An icon button that lives inside a GlassCapsule; the icon itself squashes like a droplet with a soft light bubble behind it.

props.name: icon
props.description: Ionicons glyph name.

props.name: label
props.description: Screen-reader label.

props.name: color
props.description: Tint of the icon.

components.usage: Two to four related actions that belong together — shuffle, repeat, share — floating over artwork.
components.remarks: It has no glass of its own; the surrounding GlassCapsule provides the material, so the group reads as one object.
components.a11y: `label` is required. Each button is a separate accessibility element.
examples:
<GlassCapsule>
<CapsuleButton icon="shuffle" label="Shuffle" color="#fff" onPress={shuffle} />
<CapsuleButton icon="repeat" label="Repeat" color="#fff" onPress={repeat} />
</GlassCapsule>

components.name: Chips
components.description: A scrolling row of filter chips, each with an optional count.

props.name: value
props.description: Key of the selected chip.

components.usage: Narrowing a list by one property (status, license, role). For switching between views use SegmentedControl.
components.remarks: The row scrolls horizontally when the chips do not fit; counts use the locale's number formatting.
components.a11y: Chips are tabs with a selected state.
examples: <Chips value={status} onChange={setStatus} options={[{ key: 'pending', label: 'Pending', count: 12 }, { key: 'published', label: 'Published' }]} />

components.name: ContextMenu
components.description: Long-press menu in frosted glass, opened at the touch point, with submenus.

props.name: children
props.description: The pressable to long-press; it receives `onLongPress`.

props.name: backLabel
props.description: Label of the row that leaves a submenu.

components.usage: Quick actions on an item that also has a primary tap action (a song row: tap plays, long-press shows Play next, Add to playlist, Share). Every action in the menu should also be reachable another way.
components.remarks: The child must accept `onLongPress` (ListRow, MediaTile, Pressable…). The menu is 250 points wide, clamped inside the screen; items with `children` open a submenu with a Back row. Destructive items are red.
components.a11y: The menu has the menu role and items the menuitem role; tapping the dimmed backdrop closes it.
examples:
<ContextMenu items={[
{ key: 'play', label: 'Play', icon: 'play', onPress: play },
{ key: 'add', label: 'Add to playlist', icon: 'add-circle-outline', children: playlists },
{ key: 'remove', label: 'Remove', icon: 'trash-outline', destructive: true, onPress: remove },
]}>
<ListRow title={song.title} onPress={play} />
</ContextMenu>

components.name: DatePicker
components.description: Date picker with three wheels (day, month, year) and a glass selection lens; in browsers it becomes the native date input with its calendar.

props.name: value
props.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD); '' = nothing picked yet.

props.name: max
props.description: Latest selectable date (default: today).

props.name: min
props.description: Earliest selectable date (default: 1 Jan 1900).

props.name: locale
props.description: Locale for month names (default 'en').

components.usage: Dates that are easier to scroll to than to type, such as a birth date. Bound it with `min` and `max`.
components.remarks: The value is an ISO string (YYYY-MM-DD); an empty string means nothing is picked yet. Days are clamped to the length of the month (31 January → 28 February) and the result is clamped between `min` and `max`. Month names follow `locale`.
components.a11y: Each wheel is an adjustable element: swipe up or down with a screen reader to change it, and the current value is announced.

components.name: DropletPressable
components.description: Any pressable content with the droplet press effect but no glass of its own.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessibility label (required — the content may be only an icon).

props.name: selected
props.description: Exposes a selected state to assistive technologies.

props.name: strength
props.description: How strongly the shape squashes when pressed.

components.usage: Use it for custom controls that already have their own look (a large play button, an artwork card) but should still feel like the rest of the kit when pressed.
components.remarks: Pressing squashes the content (wider, shorter); releasing bounces it back on an under-damped spring, so it overshoots and wobbles like a drop landing on glass. `strength` scales the deformation.
components.a11y: Always pass `label`: the content is often just an icon. `selected` is exposed as the accessibility selected state.

components.name: FormField
components.description: Text field with a label above it, for forms.
components.usage: Edit screens and dialogs with several fields. For a single search box use SearchField.
components.remarks: `multiline` grows the field to four lines; `keyboardType="number-pad"` for years and counts.
components.a11y: The label is also the field's accessible name.

components.name: GlassButton
components.description: Round, icon-only glass button with the droplet press effect.

props.name: icon
props.description: Ionicons glyph name.

props.name: label
props.description: Screen-reader label (required: the button has no visible text).

props.name: size
props.description: Diameter in points; keep ≥ 44 for touch targets.

props.name: variant
props.description: 'clear' glass over artwork, 'regular' elsewhere.

props.name: tint
props.description: Tinted (prominent) glass, e.g. the accent colour for a primary action.

props.name: nudge
props.description: Optical offset for glyphs that look off-centre (e.g. chevrons).

components.usage: Floating controls over content: close, back, more, add. For a labelled action use ActionButton; for several icons in one pill use GlassCapsule with CapsuleButton.
components.remarks: `tint` turns it into a prominent coloured button, `variant="clear"` suits artwork backgrounds and `tone` forces light or dark glass. `nudge` shifts asymmetric glyphs such as chevrons so they look centred.
components.a11y: `label` is required and read by screen readers. Keep `size` at 44 points or more so it stays easy to hit.

components.name: GlassCapsule
components.description: A glass pill that holds several CapsuleButtons as one compact toolbar.
components.usage: Secondary actions floating over media. Keep it short: more than four actions belong in a ContextMenu.
components.remarks: Height is 44 points with 3 points of inner padding, so CapsuleButtons sit inside with an even rim.
components.a11y: The capsule itself is not focusable; screen readers move through the buttons inside it.

components.name: SearchField
components.description: Search field with a magnifier, a clear button once something is typed, and an optional floating glass style.

props.name: glass
props.description: Renders the field as a floating glass capsule.

props.name: clearLabel
props.description: Accessibility label of the clear button.

props.name: style
props.description: Outer layout (e.g. flex: 1 inside a toolbar).

components.usage: Filtering a list or the catalog. Use `glass` when the field floats over content (for example at the bottom of the screen); keep the plain style inside a page.
components.remarks: At least 44 points tall. The clear button resets the value through `onChangeText('')`, so the parent stays the single source of truth.
components.a11y: The placeholder doubles as the accessible name; `clearLabel` names the clear button.

components.name: SegmentedControl
components.description: Switches between two to five related views. The selected segment is marked by a glass thumb that slides on a spring and stretches while it moves.

props.name: value
props.description: Key of the selected segment.

components.usage: Mutually exclusive views of the same content (Songs / Albums / Artists). For navigation between unrelated sections use a tab bar or a sidebar instead.
components.remarks: Segments share the width equally. The first layout places the thumb without animation; later changes animate.
components.a11y: The control is a tab list and each segment a tab with its selected state, so screen readers announce “tab, 2 of 3, selected”.
examples:
<SegmentedControl value={tab} onChange={setTab} segments={[
{ key: 'songs', label: 'Songs' },
{ key: 'albums', label: 'Albums' },
]} />

components.name: Spinner
components.description: Activity indicator in the accent colour.
components.usage: Short waits where the layout is already known: a button that is saving, a list that is loading its first page.
components.remarks: Wraps the platform activity indicator; every prop of it is accepted and `color` defaults to the accent colour.
components.a11y: Pair it with text or an accessibilityLabel that says what is loading.

components.name: TextField
components.description: Single-line text input with one autofill hint that works on every platform.

props.name: multiline
props.description: Grows to several lines.

props.name: secureTextEntry
props.description: Masks the input (passwords).

props.name: onSubmitEditing
props.description: Called when the Return key is pressed.

props.name: textContentType
props.description: One autofill hint for every platform: saved passwords, new-password suggestions, one-time codes from mail and SMS.

components.usage: Every form field. Set `textContentType` on sign-in, sign-up and one-time-code fields so the system password manager and code autofill can help.
components.remarks: `textContentType` is translated to each platform's autofill hint and to the HTML autocomplete attribute on the web. `onSubmitEditing` fires on the Return key.
components.a11y: Pass `accessibilityLabel` when the placeholder is the only label; placeholders disappear while typing.
examples: <TextField value={code} onChangeText={setCode} placeholder="6-digit code" keyboardType="number-pad" maxLength={6} textContentType="oneTimeCode" />

components.name: Toggle
components.description: On/off switch in the accent colour, using the platform's own switch.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: Required when there is no visible label next to the switch.

components.usage: Settings that take effect immediately. If a change needs confirmation or a Save step, use a checkbox-style row instead.
components.remarks: Wraps the native switch, so it gets the platform's haptics, animation and sizing for free.
components.a11y: Give it an `accessibilityLabel` unless a visible label sits in the same row and describes it.

components.name: BackButton
components.description: Round glass back button with a chevron, placed at the leading edge of a child screen.

props.name: label
props.description: Name of the screen you return to.

props.name: tone
props.description: Use 'dark' over dark artwork, 'light' over light artwork.

components.usage: The first control of every pushed screen. Pair it with an edge swipe so both gestures go back.
components.remarks: It is a GlassButton with the chevron optically nudged and the standard top/leading margins; override them with `style`.
components.a11y: `label` names the destination (“Library”) and is announced as the button's name.

components.name: GlassTabBar
components.description: Floating tab bar made of one glass capsule. The selection lens slides to the tapped tab on a spring, stretches while it moves and settles like a droplet; the selected tab switches to its filled icon.

props.name: value
props.description: Key of the selected tab (no lens when it matches none).

props.name: tint
props.description: Colour of the selected tab (default: accent).

components.usage: Top-level sections of an app on phones (three to five). On wide screens use NavigationSidebar.
components.remarks: Pass `iconActive` for a filled variant of each icon. When `value` matches no tab the lens is hidden — useful while a screen outside the tabs is open.
components.a11y: Announced as a tab list with each tab's selected state; tabs shrink when pressed and bounce back on release.
examples:
<GlassTabBar value={tab} onChange={setTab} items={[
{ key: 'home', label: 'Home', icon: 'home-outline', iconActive: 'home' },
{ key: 'library', label: 'Library', icon: 'albums-outline', iconActive: 'albums' },
]} />

components.name: NavigationSidebar
components.description: Sidebar of a split view: a floating glass panel with a filter field, titled sections and a tinted selection.

props.name: selected
props.description: Key of the selected item.

props.name: header
props.description: Element above the filter field (a title, a logo).

components.usage: Navigation with many destinations on wide screens — documentation, settings, a library. On phones show it as a slide-over panel opened from the navigation bar.
components.remarks: It scrolls on its own, so the content column keeps its scroll position. The filter matches labels and the optional `keywords` of each item; empty sections are hidden while filtering.
components.a11y: Sections are headers and items are buttons with a selected state.
examples:
<NavigationSidebar selected={page} onSelect={setPage} sections={[
{ items: [{ key: 'home', label: 'Home' }] },
{ title: 'Library', icon: 'albums-outline', items: [{ key: 'songs', label: 'Songs', trailing: '1,144' }] },
]} />

components.name: Sheet
components.description:
Sheet for a focused task on top of the current screen: a side panel on wide screens, a bottom sheet on phones,
with a frosted-glass header and an optional sticky footer.

props.name: footer
props.description: Sticky footer, usually the save button.

components.usage: Editing or inspecting one item without losing the list behind it (a song, a user, a room). Put the save action in `footer`.
components.remarks: At 900 points and wider it slides in from the trailing edge (560 points wide); narrower it rises from the bottom up to 92 % of the height. Tapping the dimmed backdrop or the close button calls `onClose`.
components.a11y: The close button is labelled; the system back gesture and the Escape key also close it.
examples:
<Sheet visible={!!song} title={song?.title ?? ''} subtitle={song?.artist} onClose={() => setSong(null)} footer={<ActionButton title="Save" onPress={save} />}>
<FormField label="Title" value={title} onChange={setTitle} />
</Sheet>

components.name: Artwork
components.description: Square artwork that falls back to GlassArt when there is no image or the image fails to load.
components.usage: Anywhere you show a cover. Prefer it over a bare Image so every screen handles missing covers the same way.
components.remarks: If HugoProvider has a `renderArtwork`, that renderer is used instead — one place to route every cover through a CDN or a cache.
components.a11y: Images ignore colour inversion so covers keep their real colours under smart invert.

components.name: GlassArt
components.description: Generated glass artwork for items without a cover: a translucent pane with a diagonal sheen, a bright rim and a glass bead holding the Hugo Music mark.

props.name: children
props.description: Content placed on top of the glass.

components.usage: Placeholder artwork. Artwork and MediaTile fall back to it on their own, so you rarely place it directly.
components.remarks: It is drawn without live blur so hundreds of them can scroll smoothly in long lists.
components.a11y: Decorative: it exposes no label of its own.

components.name: GradientTile
components.description: Colour card for content without artwork — generated mixes, genres, stations — with a diagonal sheen, a bright rim and its icon in a clear-glass bead.

props.name: colors
props.description: Two-stop gradient, e.g. gradientFor(key).

props.name: big
props.description: Hero typography (32 pt title).

props.name: label
props.description: Accessibility label when it differs from the title.

props.name: brand
props.description: Small wordmark in the top-right corner of big tiles.

components.usage: When there is no real cover. Feed it `gradientFor(key)` so the same item always gets the same colours.
components.remarks: White bold text is used on every gradient, so pick saturated colour pairs. `big` switches to hero typography for featured tiles.
components.a11y: The title (or `label`) is the accessible name.
examples: <GradientTile title="Chill Mix" subtitle="Made for you" colors={gradientFor('chill')} icon="shuffle" width={220} height={260} big onPress={open} />

components.name: InsetGroup
components.description: Inset grouped section in the style of a settings screen: an optional header, rows on a rounded card and an optional footer.

props.name: header
props.description: Small uppercase heading above the card.

props.name: footer
props.description: Explanatory text under the card.

props.name: style
props.description: Overrides the outer margins (default: screen gutter left/right, 24 pt above).

components.usage: Settings and forms made of rows. Put ListRows inside; use the footer to explain what a setting does.
components.remarks: The separator of the last row is removed automatically. Margins default to the screen gutter; pass `style` to change them.
components.a11y: The header is announced as a header; rows keep their own roles.
examples:
<InsetGroup header="Playback" footer="Sound Check plays every song at the same volume.">
<ListRow title="Sound Check" right={<Toggle value={on} onValueChange={setOn} accessibilityLabel="Sound Check" />} />
<ListRow title="Crossfade" subtitle="6 seconds" chevron onPress={openCrossfade} />
</InsetGroup>

components.name: LargeTitle
components.description: Large title (34 points) at the top of a screen, with an optional subtitle and trailing element.

props.name: right
props.description: Element aligned to the trailing edge (e.g. an account button).

components.usage: The first element of every top-level screen. Child screens use a BackButton and a smaller title instead.
components.remarks: Uses the content margin (`GUTTER`) so it lines up with shelves and lists below.
components.a11y: The title has the header role, so screen-reader users can jump to it.

components.name: ListRow
components.description: Standard list row: artwork or icon, title, subtitle and a trailing element, at least 56 points tall.

props.name: art
props.description: Artwork URL ('' shows the glass placeholder); takes precedence over icon.

props.name: round
props.description: Circular artwork (artists).

props.name: icon
props.description: Ionicons glyph shown when there is no artwork.

props.name: active
props.description: Highlights the row as selected or playing.

props.name: onLongPress
props.description: Long press (used by ContextMenu).

props.name: separator
props.description: Draws the hairline below the row, inset to the text like system lists.

props.name: chevron
props.description: Shows a disclosure chevron (the row opens another screen).

components.usage: Lists of songs, settings, search results. Use `chevron` when the row opens another screen and `right` for an inline control such as a Toggle.
components.remarks: The trailing element sits outside the tappable area because it usually holds its own button. The separator is inset to the text, as in system lists; InsetGroup hides it on the last row.
components.a11y: Title and subtitle are read together; `active` is exposed as selected.
examples: <ListRow icon="albums-outline" title="Albums" subtitle="18 albums" chevron onPress={open} />

components.name: MediaTile
components.description: Artwork tile with title and subtitle for shelves of songs, albums and artists. The current item shows a small glass play badge.

props.name: uri
props.description: Artwork URL.

props.name: art
props.description: Custom artwork element instead of the URL.

props.name: size
props.description: Edge length of the artwork in points.

props.name: round
props.description: Circular artwork for artists.

props.name: badge
props.description: Corner badge text, e.g. LYRICS.

props.name: active
props.description: Marks the tile as the current item (accent title + glass play badge).

props.name: playing
props.description: Shows pause instead of play on the active badge.

props.name: onLongPress
props.description: Long press (used by ContextMenu).

components.usage: Inside a Shelf or a grid. Use `round` for artists.
components.remarks: Artwork goes through Artwork (and therefore HugoProvider's `renderArtwork`) unless you pass `art`. `badge` adds a small corner label such as LYRICS.
components.a11y: Title and subtitle form the accessible name; `active` is exposed as selected.

components.name: PinnedRow
components.description: Pinned glass row for personal shortcuts at the top of a list (liked songs, downloads, the current station).

props.name: colors
props.description: Gradient of the icon square.

props.name: right
props.description: Trailing element (default: a chevron when pressable).

components.usage: One to three shortcuts above a long list. Always show them, even when empty — the subtitle tells the user how to fill them.
components.remarks: The icon sits on a gradient square; a chevron appears automatically when the row is pressable unless you pass `right`.
components.a11y: Title and subtitle are read together.
examples: <PinnedRow icon="heart" colors={['#FF375F', '#FF9F0A']} title="Liked songs" subtitle="42 songs" onPress={open} />

components.name: SectionHeader
components.description: Section heading (Title 2) that becomes a button with a chevron when it leads to a “See all” page.

props.name: onSeeAll
props.description: Makes the heading a button with a chevron.

components.usage: Above a shelf or a list section on a browsing screen.
components.remarks: Without `onSeeAll` it is a plain header; with it the whole heading is tappable, not just the chevron.
components.a11y: Header role without `onSeeAll`, button role with it.

components.name: Shelf
components.description: Horizontally scrolling row of tiles under a SectionHeader, aligned to the content margins.

props.name: gap
props.description: Space between tiles in points.

components.usage: Browsing collections — recently played, new releases, artists. Put MediaTile or GradientTile inside.
components.remarks: The first tile lines up with the screen margin and the row scrolls past the edge, hinting that more is available.
components.a11y: Tiles stay individually focusable; the shelf title is the section's header.
examples:
<Shelf title="Recently played" onSeeAll={openAll}>
{songs.map((s) => <MediaTile key={s.id} uri={s.cover} title={s.title} size={150} onPress={() => play(s)} />)}
</Shelf>

components.name: Badge
components.description: Short status label in a soft colour pill.
components.usage: One- or two-word states next to an item: Published, Pending, Admin only. Use the same tone for the same meaning everywhere.
components.remarks: Six tones (green, red, amber, blue, violet, gray) with colours tuned for each appearance; an optional icon sits before the text.
components.a11y: The label is read as text; do not rely on the colour alone to carry meaning.

components.name: BarChart
components.description: Minimal bar chart: one bar per data point, labels at both ends of the axis.
components.usage: Small trends on dashboards (plays per day, uploads per week). For precise values show a table next to it.
components.remarks: Bars scale to the largest value; zero values stay visible as a thin line. No chart dependency is needed.
components.a11y: Every bar has an accessibility label with its label and value.
examples: <BarChart height={60} data={days.map((d) => ({ label: d.label, value: d.plays }))} />

components.name: Card
components.description: Content card with an optional title row (title, subtitle, trailing element).

props.name: right
props.description: Element at the trailing edge of the title row.

props.name: padded
props.description: Set false for edge-to-edge lists inside the card.

components.usage: Grouping related content on dashboards and edit pages. For settings-style rows prefer InsetGroup.
components.remarks: A solid surface with a hairline border — cards hold content, so they are not glass. `padded={false}` lets lists run edge to edge inside.
components.a11y: The title is plain text; give it a header role in your own layout when it starts a section.

components.name: EmptyState
components.description: Placeholder for an empty list or a search without results: an icon, a title and a hint.
components.usage: Whenever a list can be empty. Say what is missing and, in the hint, how to fill it.
components.remarks: Centred, with generous vertical padding so it reads as a state rather than an error.
components.a11y: Title and hint are read as text.
examples: <EmptyState icon="search-outline" title="Nothing matches" hint="Try another filter" />

components.name: ErrorText
components.description: Inline error message on a soft red background; renders nothing when the message is empty.
components.usage: Under a form or above a table when loading or saving failed. Say what went wrong and what to do next.
components.remarks: Pass the error message straight from a failed request; `null` or `''` hides it.
components.a11y: The message is announced as an alert when it appears.

components.name: Pager
components.description: Previous / next pagination with “page x of y · n items”.

props.name: page
props.description: Current page, starting at 1.

props.name: total
props.description: Number of items across all pages.

props.name: limit
props.description: Items per page.

props.name: labels
props.type: { previous: string; next: string; page: string; items: string; }
props.default: { previous: 'Previous page', next: 'Next page', page: 'Page', items: 'items' }

components.usage: Under long server-paginated tables. Renders nothing when everything fits on one page.
components.remarks: Pages are 1-based; the buttons disable themselves at the ends. `labels` localises the text.
components.a11y: The arrow buttons are named Previous page and Next page.

components.name: StatCard
components.description: Metric card: a tinted icon, a large number, a label and an optional hint.

props.name: hint
props.description: Small coloured line under the label, e.g. a trend.

components.usage: Dashboard numbers that lead somewhere — tapping a card can open the filtered list behind the number.
components.remarks: Numbers use locale formatting. Cards grow to fill a wrapping row (about four per row on wide screens).
components.a11y: Pressable cards are buttons named by their label and value.
examples: <StatCard icon="time-outline" tone="amber" label="Awaiting review" value={12} onPress={openQueue} />

components.name: AccountButton
components.description: Round avatar button in the top-right of a tab; opens the account screen or the sign-in sheet.

components.name: SongList
components.description: A list of songs rendered as SongRow items; tapping a row plays the song with the list as the queue.

props.name: subtitle
props.description: Builds each row's subtitle; defaults to the artist.

props.name: onPlay
props.description: Overrides the default play behaviour.

props.name: onRemove
props.description: When set, the row menu offers “Remove from this list”.

components.name: SongRow
components.description: One song in a list: artwork, title, artist and a “…” menu. Prefer SongList for whole arrays of songs.

props.name: list
props.description: Queue used when the row is played.

props.name: last
props.description: Hides the separator below the last row.

props.name: subtitle
props.description: Builds each row's subtitle; defaults to the artist.

props.name: onPlay
props.description: Overrides the default play behaviour.

props.name: onRemove
props.description: When set, the row menu offers “Remove from this list”.

components.name: SwipeBack
components.description: Wraps a child screen so a swipe from the leading edge goes back.

props.name: onBack
props.description: Called when the swipe passes the threshold.

components.name: BottomPlayer
components.description: Mini player docked above the tab bar: current song, play/pause and next; expands to the full player.

props.name: onOpenFullPlayer
props.description: Opens the full-screen player.

props.name: onOpenLyrics
props.description: Opens the lyrics panel.

components.name: BottomTabBar
components.description: Bottom tab bar for phones (Home, New, Radio, Library, Search).

props.name: activeTab
props.description: Id of the selected tab.

props.name: onTabChange
props.description: Called with the id of the tapped tab.

components.name: CollectionDetail
components.description: Full detail screen for an album, playlist, chart or mix: hero artwork, actions and the song list.

props.name: kind
props.description: Kind of collection; drives labels and the hero layout.

props.name: about
props.description: Optional description shown under the title.

props.name: onRemoveSong
props.description: Enables removing songs (playlists).

props.name: numbered
props.description: Shows track numbers instead of artwork.

props.name: onMoveSong
props.description: Shows up/down controls to reorder songs.

components.name: CoverArt
components.description: Song or album cover. Loads through the CDN and falls back to generated artwork — never an empty square.

props.name: title
props.description: Used to generate artwork when there is no cover.

props.name: uri
props.description: Cover URL (R2 URLs are rewritten to the CDN).

props.name: fallbackUri
props.description: Second image to try before the generated artwork.

components.name: LicenseBadge
components.description: Small license label under a song title (CC BY, Public Domain…). Attribution is a legal requirement of these licenses, not decoration; labels come from /api/meta.

components.name: LyricsSidePanel
components.description: Side panel with time-synced lyrics next to the player on wide screens.

props.name: onExpandFullScreen
props.description: Switches to full-screen lyrics.

components.name: SeekBar
components.description: Draggable progress/volume bar working on a 0–1 ratio (tap or drag).

props.name: progress
props.description: Current value between 0 and 1.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables seeking, e.g. for live radio.

props.name: label
props.description: Screen-reader label (required).

examples: <SeekBar progress={position / duration} onSeek={(r) => seek(r * duration)} trackColor={colors.fill} fillColor={colors.accent} label="Song progress" />

components.name: Sidebar
components.description: Left navigation sidebar for tablets and desktop web.

props.name: activeTab
props.description: Id of the selected tab.

props.name: onTabChange
props.description: Called with the id of the tapped tab.

components.name: SongActionsHost
components.description: Mounts the shared song action sheet (add to playlist, like, share) once at the app root.

components.name: SongMenu
components.description: Wraps a trigger element and opens the song action menu for one song.

props.name: onRemove
props.description: Adds “Remove from this list” to the menu.

components.name: UserAvatar
components.description: User avatar: uploaded photo, the sign-in provider photo or generated initials, with an optional badge.

props.name: fallbackBg
props.description: Background colour behind the initials.

props.name: badge
props.description: Element shown at the bottom-right (e.g. an admin mark).
